stem: A client with acute ischemic stroke is admitted to an organized inpatient stroke unit rather than a general medical ward. Which outcome is most consistent with current evidence?

options.A: Greater likelihood of survival, independence, and living at home after follow-up because organized stroke-unit care integrates specialized multidisciplinary assessment, treatment, and rehabilitation.
options.B: No meaningful difference in survival or independence compared with conventional ward care once acute reperfusion decisions are complete.
options.C: Worse functional outcomes because geographically colocated stroke units delay rehabilitation and multidisciplinary care.
options.D: A shorter hospital stay is the main proven benefit, whereas mortality and disability outcomes are unchanged.

rationale: A is correct. The 2026 AHA/ASA acute ischemic stroke guideline states that organized inpatient stroke-unit care reduces death, disability, and institutionalization. The supporting systematic review found that patients cared for in organized stroke units were more likely to survive, be independent, and live at home at follow-up; benefits were seen across age, sex, stroke type, and severity. B and C contradict this evidence. D is incorrect because the guideline notes no clear effect on length of stay while showing better survival and independence outcomes.
educational_objective: Recognize organized inpatient stroke-unit care as a multidisciplinary care model associated with improved survival, independence, and discharge/home-living outcomes compared with conventional ward care.
source_organization: American Heart Association / American Stroke Association
source_document_title: 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke
source_locator: Section 5.1 Stroke Units — Synopsis: organized stroke-unit care reduces death, disability, and institutionalization; key characteristics include specialized multidisciplinary care, caregiver involvement, staff specialization, early/intensive therapy, and treatment protocols. Recommendation-Specific Supportive Text: updated systematic review of 29 trials/5902 participants found patients in organized inpatient stroke units more likely to survive, be independent, and live at home, with no clear effect on length of stay.
source_claim_supported: Organized inpatient stroke-unit care improves clinically important outcomes such as survival and independence relative to conventional ward care and is characterized by coordinated specialized multidisciplinary management.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: coordinate interdisciplinary care, use specialized resources, and support evidence-based systems that improve client outcomes.
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — organized stroke-unit care
correction_summary: Rebuilt the raw outcome statement against the 2026 AHA/ASA stroke-unit evidence and corrected the blueprint from Safety & Infection Prevention and Control to Management of Care. Removed the unsupported causal simplification that outcomes improve solely because of protocols/staff expertise and instead used the guideline-supported organized multidisciplinary care model.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: Verified directly against Section 5.1 of the 2026 AHA/ASA acute ischemic stroke guideline.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: A matches the systematic-review outcomes and stroke-unit model. B denies documented benefit. C reverses the evidence. D incorrectly makes shorter length of stay the main benefit.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct; improved survival, independence, and home-living outcomes.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; organized stroke-unit care improves outcomes beyond reperfusion decisions alone.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; geographically colocated organized units show strong benefit.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; length of stay was not the demonstrated primary benefit.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A accurately combines the outcome evidence with the organized multidisciplinary care construct.
audit_findings.cueing: All options compare clinically relevant outcomes of stroke-unit versus general-ward care.
audit_findings.blueprint: Interdisciplinary coordination and specialized care systems fit Management of Care.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked survival, independence, home-living, length-of-stay, and colocation findings in the 2026 guideline. Avoided claiming one isolated component explains the full effect. No second defensible answer remained.
